newsitem.title: USA: Texaco's chief says bonuses may be cut - letter.
newsitem.headline: Texaco's chief says bonuses may be cut - letter.

text.p: Texaco Inc Chief Executive Peter Bijur told California state Treasurer Matt Fong that executives who "acted inappropriately" could lose all or part of their bonus awards, Fong said on Tuesday.
In November, Fong urged Texaco's board of directors to withhold or cut annual bonuses given to company executives in response to the company's discrimination scandal.
Texaco settled a civil suit charging discrimination in November with black employees for $115 million.
Fong also asked the state's pension employee retirement funds, which hold about two million shares of Texaco stock, to put pressure on Texaco to take action.

In his response, received by Fong on Tuesday, Bijur told the state treasurer that "those individuals who have acted inappropriately and bear responsibility for reprehensible conduct will be disciplined accordingly including the loss of all, or part of, their cash bonus awards."
Bijur's letter warned against "indiscriminately" withholding or reducing bonuses to punish "good people."
